premise: At 57, after 29 years as a 911 dispatcher, I discovered my adult son had drained my $143,000 457(b) retirement account by forging a hardship-distribution request to buy a fleet of party bikes, leaving me with a $4,300 'corrective refund' notice. I proved the signature was forged by a handwriting analyst, got the plan administrator to reverse the distribution, seized the bikes as restitution, and now run 'Pedal of Deceit Party Bike Tours,' where he greases chains in a shirt that says 'Grifter on Board' and every rental ticket prints his fraud-docket number.
